purpose: Decide whether seven catalogue entries whose data may live in small public GitHub repositories are actually present as pinnable files.

method.github_api: unauthenticated (60 requests/hour): commits/HEAD, git/trees?recursive=1, repo metadata, branches, commit details for deep-image-prior's data/ history; repository and user searches for VIA-Bench
method.raw_fetches: raw.githubusercontent.com at the pinned commit: READMEs, LICENSE files, data.json, the group-words JSON, 6+3 notebooks as text; arXiv abstract page; Hugging Face public JSON API (papers, dataset/model/space search); two project web pages; S3 HEAD and 1-byte ranged GET
not_done: no image was opened, viewed or decoded
no dataset content was sent to any model or external service
no clone, no LFS, no archive download

bytes_transferred.note: Raw file sizes are exact response sizes; GitHub/HF API JSON was not metered per request and is estimated from the saved responses.

outcome.summary: None of the seven populations is present as pinnable files, so no recipe, preview, index or test was written; every entry carries dated source_audit evidence and one appended blocker line. All seven stay identity candidate and publication not_reviewed.

blocker_classification: Each is an external blocker (the population is not published as a public pinnable file, or its host denies access). None is an implementation gap: no format needs an adapter.
limits: Only the repositories named by each entry were audited; the pictures' other origins (for example Heide et al. for the 11 inpainting images, Charlesworth et al. for the group-label lexicon) were not searched.
Git history was enumerated only for deep-image-prior's data/ directory; for the other repositories the repo size field is cited as corroboration, not proof.
S3 403 cannot distinguish a removed object from a private one; either way nothing is publicly retrievable.
Absence on 2026-10-09 is not a statement about later releases; refresh by pinned file.
